newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Van Miert urges settlement of VW row.
newsitem.headline: Van Miert urges settlement of VW row.

text.p: Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert warned on Wednesday that time was running out to solve a crisis triggered by the illegal payment of subsidies to Volkswagen AG.

Van Miert said a compromise struck with the German government in September, which neutralised 90 million marks paid by the state of Saxony despite Commission opposition, could be brought into question at the end of 1996.
This was because the German government had only committed itself to blocking an equivalent amount of authorised subsidies until the end of the year, Van Miert told reporters.
At that point Volkswagen could call on the German government to grant the aid in the form of tax rebates.
"The more we approach the end of the year, the hotter this story gets," Van Miert said.

In a move to avoid another confrontation with the German authorities, he indicated that Volkswagen could shut down production capacity elsewhere in Germany to the equivalent of 300 cars a year produced in its Saxony plant.

Earlier this year the Commission prohibited the payment of 240 million marks out of a total 780 million marks in subsidies promised to Volksagen to fund investment projects at its plants in Chemnitz and Mosel, in Saxony.
